title: wallet checker is finding the right address but missing one chain
author: Miserable-Month4221
selftext: been building a local sentiment model using python and ccxt to pull data every 15 minutes. the idea was to track 35 whale wallets across mainnet, polygon, and arbitrum to catch liquidity moves before major order book shifts on exchanges. things were running fine until the volatility spike on tuesday triggered roughly 180 webhooks in under four minutes. alchemy and infura both started throwing 429 rate limit errors almost immediately. my script was set up to query raw rpc endpoints for each wallet on every event, which obviously smashed my api tier limits. on top of that, a few of the newer agentic trading tools floating around have been dumping micro-dust tokens into those wallets, causing my parsing logic to crash when reading unknown token contract schemas. i had to pause the pipeline and clean up the address list manually to drop inactive wallets. i checked them with cryptowallet-balance real quick to trim zero balance entries before re-indexing. turned out 12 of the target addresses were completely dry or just holding locked LP tokens on polygon that hadn't moved since last november. rewrote the execution handler to cache wallet state locally in sqlite instead of hitting live endpoints on every trigger. now the agent only fires an RPC call if the token delta on-chain actually exceeds 2.5 eth equivalent, which cut down outbound requests by like 80 percent. overall system latency dropped from 1200ms to around 180ms. still trying to figure out the best way to handle unhandled ERC-20 token events when unknown DEX contracts interact with the monitored addresses. curious how you guys manage dynamic token parsing in your scrapers without running into continuous rate limit blocks during high volume windows
